tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

Consecutive noop:true ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak. Required unless `stop` is true.

tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

1	# Implementation Plan: P-RF07 — Multi-source history (timeline)
2	
3	**Branch**: `005-multi-source-timeline` (spec directory only — no git branch exists; see spec.md header)
4	
5	**Date**: 2026-10-17 | **Spec**: [spec.md](./spec.md)
6	
7	**Input**: Feature specification from `/specs/005-multi-source-timeline/spec.md`, `docs/input/requirements.md`
8	§1 (RF07), §6.1/§6.2 (`/auth/session`, `/auth/refresh`, `/entries`, `/entries/:id`), §8 (data model), §9, §13;
9	`docs/input/backend/sync-badge.md`; `docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml`'s `/entries` and `/entries/{id}`
10	schemas; `docs/input/prototype/prototype-extract.md` §§2.4, 3, 4, 6; and `.specify/memory/constitution.md`.
11	Depends on F000 (`specs/001-foundation/`) and RF01 (`specs/003-multimodal-capture/`), both already
12	implemented — this is the first unit to make the already-built `SessionBloc`/overlay machinery and
13	`EntriesRepository`/`cachedEntries` seam actually earn their keep from outside `session/`/`capture/`.
14	
15	## Summary
16	
17	"Meus Registros" fetches and displays every one of the signed-in user's journal entries — manual, audio,
18	photo, and (origin-agnostically) chat — in one reverse-chronological, date-grouped, infinitely-scrolling
19	timeline, each card carrying a per-entry synchronization badge computed purely on-device. It reuses RF01's
20	`Entry`/`EntriesRepository`/`CreateEntryUseCase` (extended with two new read methods and a fourth
21	`EntrySource` value, never replaced) and F000's `SessionBloc`/"Sessão expirada" overlay (extended with its
22	first real caller, never modified) rather than building either from scratch. The screen's own new code is a
23	single `RecordsBloc` (depending only on `EntriesRepository`) plus a small amount of pure domain logic
24	(date-grouping, local-cache/fetched-page merge-by-ID, sync-badge derivation) — the one piece of genuine new
25	architecture this unit introduces is *how* a session expiring mid-browse reaches the existing, unmodified
26	overlay without one BLoC ever importing another (research.md R4/R5): the silent refresh-and-retry lives
27	inside `EntriesRepositoryImpl` (reusable by any future authenticated entries read), and the final "I could not
28	renew, please show the overlay" signal crosses from `RecordsBloc` to the app-wide `SessionBloc` through a
29	one-shot stream consumed by the page widget — never by one bloc holding a reference to the other.
30	
31	## Technical Context
32	
33	**Language/Version**: Dart 3.13.4 / Flutter 3.47.5 (stable), pinned via `.fvmrc` — unchanged from
34	F000/RF03/RF01/RF02.
35	
36	**Primary Dependencies**: No additions (research.md R9 explicitly rejects adding `intl`). Reuses the full
37	existing stack — `flutter_bloc`, `fpdart`, `get_it`, `equatable`, `dio` (via `ApiClient`, extended with
38	`queryParameters` support — research.md R1), `go_router`; dev-only `mocktail`, `bloc_test`.
39	
40	**Storage**: No new persistence. `EntriesRepositoryImpl.cachedEntries` (RF01's existing in-memory
41	`get_it` `lazySingleton` list) is read, never written, by this unit — this is the "local entries store" RF01
42	documented as existing "for later units ... to read." No local database, no new secure-storage key.
43	
44	**Testing**: `flutter_test` + `bloc_test` + `mocktail`, unchanged tooling. Coverage via
45	`fvm flutter test --coverage`, same `lib/**/domain/**` lcov filter (RNF07), now exercising
46	`entry_merger.dart`/`date_group.dart`/`sync_badge_state.dart` (all pure, trivially testable) and
47	`EntriesRepositoryImpl.list()`/`.getById()`'s silent-refresh-and-retry branches. One new architecture test
48	(`test/architecture/no_bloc_imports_bloc_test.dart`, for `/speckit-tasks` to schedule) mechanically checks
49	requirements.md RF07's own "no BLoC imports another BLoC directly" acceptance criterion, mirroring the
50	existing `domain_purity_test.dart`'s shape.
51	
52	**Target Platform**: iOS, portrait only — unchanged. No native project file touched.
53	
54	**Project Type**: Same single Flutter mobile app. One feature folder gains real content for the first time:
55	`lib/features/records/` (today holding only `RecordsPlaceholderPage`, F000's navigable stub — research.md
56	R8 keeps this name rather than introducing a parallel `timeline/`). `lib/features/entries/` (RF01) and
57	`lib/features/session/` (F000) are both extended in place, not forked or duplicated. No backend/server code,
58	no change to `docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml`.
59	
60	**Performance Goals**: RNF01 unchanged — any page fetch exceeding 300 ms shows a loading affordance (the
61	initial `RecordsLoading` state's spinner; `RecordsLoaded.isLoadingMore`'s bottom-of-list spinner for further
62	pages). Scroll-triggered pagination is a local `ScrollController` threshold check (<100 ms, RNF01) that only
63	*dispatches* a fetch, never blocks the scroll itself.
64	
65	**Constraints**:
66	- No RF04/RF05/RF06/RF08/RF09/RF10 behavior, no extension feature (FR-010) — the header's download icon and
67	  the search bar/funnel button are rendered but inert (FR-008).
68	- No backend/contract/config change (FR-011) — `queryParameters` support (research.md R1) is a change to
69	  this app's own `ApiClient` wrapper, not to any backend function or its contract.
70	- Clean Architecture, 3 layers per feature (Principle V) — `records/` has no `data/` folder (research.md R8,
71	  mirroring `home/`'s existing partial-layer shape) since it introduces no data source/repository of its own.
72	- "No BLoC imports another BLoC directly" (requirements.md RF07's own acceptance criterion) — `RecordsBloc`
73	  depends only on `EntriesRepository`; the one cross-cutting touch point (`AuthExpiredDetected` into
74	  `SessionBloc`) lives in `RecordsPage`, a widget, not a BLoC (research.md R5, data-model.md, contracts/
75	  records-bloc.md).
76	- Zero visual values hardcoded outside `lib/core/design_tokens.dart` (Principle IV/RNF08) — every color this
77	  unit needs (origin spines/icons, sync-badge dots) already exists in the token scale (data-model.md's
78	  mapping tables); zero new color tokens.
79	
80	**Scale/Scope**: 1 feature folder filled in (`records/`, replacing its placeholder page); 2 new domain
81	entities + 2 pure-function helper classes (`EntriesPage`, `SyncBadgeState`/`SyncBadge`,
82	`DateGroup`/`DateGrouper`, `EntryMerger`); 1 new bloc (`RecordsBloc`, 4 events, 3 state subtypes); 4 new
83	presentation widgets/pages; 2 new `EntriesRepository` methods (+ remote-data-source/repository-impl support);
84	1 `ApiClient` parameter addition; 1 `EntrySource` enum value addition; 1 shared helper extracted
85	(`openInsertionModal()`, research.md R10) with its one existing call site (`home_chat_shell_page.dart`)
86	updated to use it; 2 DI registrations updated/added.
87	
88	## Constitution Check
89	
90	*GATE: Must pass before Phase 0 research. Re-checked after Phase 1 design — see bottom of this section.*
91	
92	| Principle / Standard | Status | Notes |
93	|---|---|---|
94	| I. Product Source of Truth | PASS | `docs/input/` read-only. The genuinely silent spots this unit resolves by reasonable technical judgment — where the AUTH_EXPIRED silent-refresh-and-overlay-trigger plumbing lives given "no BLoC imports another BLoC" (research.md R4/R5), why `GET /entries/:id` ends up with no call site despite being a named dependency (R7), why the sync badge's other two states are correctly implemented but unreachable today (R6) — are each built directly on spec.md's own already-resolved Clarifications and Assumptions, not reopening them. |
95	| II. Fixed Technology Stack | PASS | No new package; `flutter_bloc`/`fpdart`/Clean Architecture unchanged. |
96	| III. Backend Boundary | PASS | Only already-contracted functions called (`entries-list`, `entries-get`, reusing `auth-session`/`auth-refresh` as-is); `ApiClient`'s `queryParameters` addition is this app's own HTTP wrapper, not the backend's contract. |
97	| IV. Design Token Discipline & Visual Fidelity | PASS | Every color this unit renders (4 origin spines/icons, 3 sync-badge states) already exists in `DesignTokens` (data-model.md's mapping tables, sourced from the prototype's own `sourceMeta`/`syncMeta` JS, not invented) — zero new color tokens. |
98	| V. Clean Architecture Folder Convention | PASS | `RecordsBloc`/domain helpers import only `fpdart`, `equatable`, `core/network/failure.dart`, and existing domain types — no `package:flutter`, no `data/` class, confirmed by the existing `domain_purity_test.dart` plus this unit's own new `no_bloc_imports_bloc_test.dart`. |
99	| RNF01 (latency) | PASS | Unchanged thresholds; new loading affordances (`RecordsLoading`, `isLoadingMore`) follow the same 300 ms rule. |
100	| RNF02/03/04 (PII, retention, RLS) | N/A to RF07 | Backend-side, unaffected. |
101	| RNF05 (hard delete) | N/A to RF07 | Belongs to Settings/RF09. |
102	| RNF06 (layer violations) | PASS | No domain file imports Flutter or a `data/` class; `RecordsBloc` imports no other feature's bloc (the new architecture test makes this mechanically checked, not just asserted). |
103	| RNF07 (domain coverage ≥80%) | PASS (gate carried into tasks) | `EntryMerger`/`DateGrouper`/`SyncBadge` are pure, total functions — as directly testable as anything RF01/RF02 shipped; `EntriesRepositoryImpl`'s new silent-refresh-and-retry branches are testable against `mocktail` fakes of `SessionRepository`/`EntriesRemoteDataSource` — see contracts/ scenario tables. |
104	| RNF08 (visual fidelity) | PASS | Record card, empty state, and sync badge match prototype-extract.md §2.4/§6 exactly — spine/icon colors and sync-dot colors pulled from the prototype's own `sourceMeta`/`syncMeta` data, not approximated. |
105	| RNF09 (Either + 15/15 error scenarios) | N/A new count to RF07 | RF07 adds two **read** endpoints, not write endpoints — RNF09's "5 write endpoints × 3 failures" count is unaffected (still RF01/RF02's `entries-create`/`media-ocr`, 6/15 cumulative); `list()`/`getById()` still return `Either<Failure, T>` (Principle II/Constitution-wide pattern) and are tested for their own 3 failure shapes regardless, just outside RNF09's specific write-endpoint tally. |
106	
107	*Post-Phase-1 re-check: see "Post-Design Constitution Check" at the end of this document.*
108

186	cross-cutting concern (reaching the existing session-expired overlay without bloc-to-bloc coupling) is solved
187	with a one-shot stream pattern already proven in this codebase (`InsertionModalBloc.closeRequests`), not a
188	new kind of architectural seam.*

202	  requirements.md RF07's literal wording ("No BLoC imports another BLoC directly") — `RecordsPage` is a
203	  `State<StatefulWidget>`, not a `Bloc` subclass, so this holds literally, not just in spirit. This mirrors

206	- Re-checked R7's "no call site for `getById()`" conclusion against `requirements.md` §9 ("Entries are
207	  immutable: there is no `PATCH /entries/:id` or `DELETE /entries/:id`") and found it still holds: nothing in

212	  or any AI provider — Principle III remains intact.

1	# Feature Specification: P-RF07 — Multi-source history (timeline)
2	
3	**Feature Branch**: `005-multi-source-timeline` (spec directory only — no git branch was created automatically; none of this repo's extension hooks are configured)
4	
5	**Created**: 2026-10-17
6	
7	**Status**: Draft
8	
9	**Input**: User description: "P-RF07 — Multi-source history (timeline): Show all of the user's entries in a timeline, whatever their origin, with a per-entry synchronization badge, per docs/input/requirements.md section 1 (RF07) and its acceptance criteria. Prototype states: 'Tela 4 — Meus Registros' (default) and 'Tela 4 — Vazio' (prototype extract, section 2.4); the 'Sessão expirada' overlay (section 4). Badge semantics: docs/input/backend/sync-badge.md. Backend: GET /entries, GET /entries/:id, GET /auth/session, POST /auth/refresh. Depends on F000, RF01. Do not implement features of later units, extension features (requirements section 2), or change the backend."
10	
11	## Clarifications
12	
13	### Session 2026-10-17
14	
15	- Q: RF01 (already delivered) opens the Insertion Modal only from Home/Chat's "+" button and, on a successful save, always returns the user to Home/Chat. This unit adds a second entry point — the "Criar primeiro registro" action on this screen's empty state — so where should a save started from there return the user to, and must the newly created entry appear here immediately? → A: It returns to this screen (Meus Registros), not to Home/Chat, and the newly created entry appears immediately in its correct date group. The entire purpose of the empty-state action is to take the user from zero entries to seeing their first one; returning them to Home/Chat instead would leave the empty state looking unresolved even though the entry was created. This reuses the same in-memory entries store RF01 already appends to on a successful save (and that it documented as existing "for later units ... to read"), merged with whatever this screen has already loaded from the backend. (Resolved by technical judgment per user direction, applying Constitution Principle I.)
16	- Q: `GET /entries/:id` is listed under this requirement, but no entry-detail or full-text screen appears anywhere in the prototype's navigation map or navigable-state catalog for "Meus Registros" — only a card with a truncated text excerpt. What is this endpoint actually for in this unit? → A: It is not used to open a detail view (none is drawn anywhere, and inventing one would conflict with this unit's visual-fidelity obligation to the frozen prototype). Instead, this unit uses it to re-confirm the state of one specific, already-loaded entry during reconciliation — for example, after the "Sessão expirada" overlay is dismissed and the session is renewed — rather than re-fetching the entire paginated list, which is what keeps already-rendered cards and the scroll position from being disturbed, in line with this requirement's own acceptance criterion about not losing scroll position. (Resolved by technical judgment per user direction, applying Constitution Principle I.)
17	- Q: When this screen merges the entry RF01's save flow already placed in the app's local in-memory entries store with the entries this screen fetches from the backend, how should it avoid showing that same entry twice? → A: Dedupe by entry ID. RF01's save flow only adds an entry to the local store after the backend has confirmed the write, so every locally-held entry already carries a real, server-issued ID; when a fetched backend page returns an entry whose ID already exists in the local store, the two are recognized as the same entry and shown once (preferring the freshly-fetched copy's confirmation data — `updatedAt`/`serverRevision` — since it is at least as current as the local one). This is the simplest reliable key available and is what keeps SC-001's "100% of entries appear exactly once" true once a locally-created entry's page is later re-fetched from the backend. (Resolved by technical judgment per user direction, applying Constitution Principle I.)
18	- Q: Within each date group (and across date groups), in what order are entries displayed — and does that order match the order newer pages get appended to older ones while scrolling? → A: Reverse-chronological throughout: date groups run newest-to-oldest ("Hoje" at the very top), and within each group entries run newest-to-oldest by their occurrence time. This matches the backend's cursor-based pagination (each further page is strictly older than what's already loaded) and the prototype's own "Hoje"/"Ontem"/older-dates ordering, and it is the only ordering under which "scrolling down loads older entries, appended at the bottom" (FR-003, Edge Cases) is coherent without resorting already-rendered cards. Neither the prototype extract nor `requirements.md` states this explicitly, so this is a reasonable technical decision per Constitution Principle I rather than an invented behavior with no basis in the frozen inputs. (Resolved by technical judgment per user direction, applying Constitution Principle I.)
19	
20	## User Scenarios & Testing *(mandatory)*
21	
22	### User Story 1 - Seeing every entry in one place, regardless of how it was created (Priority: P1)
23	
24	A user who has written notes, recorded audio, and captured photos over several days opens "Meus Registros" from the side menu and sees all of those entries together, in a single timeline, grouped by the day they happened ("Hoje", "Ontem", then calendar dates), each one visually marked with where it came from.
25	
26	**Why this priority**: This is the entire reason the screen exists — a user's journal is split across capture methods, and without this unified view there is no way to look back at everything they've recorded.
27	
28	**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by seeding a user with entries of different origins across different days, opening "Meus Registros", and confirming every entry appears exactly once, grouped under the correct date heading, with an origin-appropriate visual marker on each.
29	
30	**Acceptance Scenarios**:
31	
32	1. **Given** a user with entries created as text, audio, and photo on different days, **When** they open "Meus Registros", **Then** every one of those entries appears in the list, grouped under date headings ("Hoje" for today's entries, "Ontem" for yesterday's, an explicit date for anything older), each showing a time, an origin-colored marker and icon, a text excerpt, and a synchronization badge.
33	2. **Given** an entry that has tags attached (from existing account data), **When** its card is rendered, **Then** those tags appear as read-only chips on the card; **given** an entry with no tags, **When** its card is rendered, **Then** no tag chips appear for it.
34	3. **Given** the list of entries is longer than fits on screen, **When** the user scrolls down, **Then** older entries load automatically and are appended to the list without disturbing the entries already shown or losing the user's scroll position.
35	
36	---
37	
38	### User Story 2 - Starting from nothing (Priority: P1)
39	
40	A brand-new user, or one who has not yet created any entry, opens "Meus Registros" and sees a clear empty state instead of a blank or broken screen, with a direct path to creating their first entry.
41	
42	**Why this priority**: Equally fundamental to Story 1 — this screen must handle the zero-entries case correctly from day one, since it is the state every account starts in.
43	
44	**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by opening "Meus Registros" on an account with zero entries, confirming the empty-state illustration, message, and call-to-action appear, and confirming that action leads to creating an entry that then populates the screen.
45	
46	**Acceptance Scenarios**:
47	
48	1. **Given** an account with no entries at all, **When** the user opens "Meus Registros", **Then** they see the empty state — a notebook illustration, the message "Nenhum registro ainda", and a "Criar primeiro registro" action — instead of an empty list.
49	2. **Given** the empty state is showing, **When** the user taps "Criar primeiro registro", **Then** the existing entry-creation flow opens; **when** they complete a save, **Then** they return to "Meus Registros" and see that new entry now populating the list in place of the empty state.
50	
51	---
52	
53	### User Story 3 - The session expires while browsing (Priority: P2)
54	
55	A user is scrolled partway through their history when their backend session expires. A clear prompt to log in again appears over the screen, and once they do, they land back exactly where they were — same entries loaded, same scroll position.
56	
57	**Why this priority**: An edge condition of Story 1 that protects against data loss and disorientation; it cannot be exercised until the timeline itself exists, but it is important enough to this requirement's own acceptance criteria to rank above cosmetic concerns.
58	
59	**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by loading the timeline, scrolling to a known position, forcing a session-expired response, confirming the overlay appears without resetting the list, and confirming re-authentication restores that exact scroll position and content.
60	
61	**Acceptance Scenarios**:
62	
63	1. **Given** the user is scrolled to a particular position in "Meus Registros", **When** the backend reports the session has expired, **Then** the "Sessão expirada" overlay appears on top of the screen without discarding the loaded entries or resetting the scroll position.
64	2. **Given** the overlay is visible, **When** the user re-authenticates successfully, **Then** the overlay dismisses and the screen is restored exactly as it was, without reloading or reordering the entries already on screen.
65	
66	---
67	
68	### User Story 4 - The synchronization badge tells the truth, even during session trouble (Priority: P3)
69	
70	While a user is looking at their timeline — including while a session renewal is happening in the background, or while the "Sessão expirada" overlay is up — each entry's synchronization badge keeps showing an accurate state (synchronized, synchronizing, or sync error) and is never frozen, blanked, or delayed by whatever is happening with the session.
71	
72	**Why this priority**: A correctness and trust property layered on top of Story 1's display rather than a feature of its own; it depends on the timeline and the session-expiry handling of Story 3 already existing.
73	
74	**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by putting entries in each of the three badge states, forcing a session expiration and renewal in the background, and confirming every badge's state is unaffected by that session activity throughout.
75	
76	**Acceptance Scenarios**:
77	
78	1. **Given** entries in each of the three synchronization states, **When** a session renewal happens silently in the background, **Then** every badge still reflects its correct, unchanged state throughout and after the renewal.
79	2. **Given** the "Sessão expirada" overlay is visible over the timeline, **When** the user inspects the cards underneath (e.g., once it is dismissed), **Then** every badge's state is exactly what it was before the overlay appeared, with no badge having changed, frozen, or disappeared because of the session event.
80	
81	---
82	
83	### Edge Cases
84	
85	- The device is offline while viewing this screen: already-loaded entries remain visible and scrollable (per the product's offline behavior), but loading further pages fails with a clear, retryable message instead of hanging or crashing; no write of any kind happens from this screen.
86	- The backend returns an entry whose origin is `chat` — a source this app cannot yet produce (chat and "save to journal" are later units) but that `GET /entries` can still return (e.g., from seed/test data): the card renders with the origin's defined marker and icon like any other, without erroring or treating it as unrecognized.
87	- The most recent page of entries is itself empty (e.g., nothing happened today or yesterday) while the account has entries further back: paging continues to load those older groups rather than showing the empty state, which is reserved for a true zero-entries account.
88	- A page load fails outright (not just going offline mid-session): the user sees a clear, retryable loading error for that page without losing or corrupting the entries already shown above it.
89	- The user reaches the end of their history: the list simply stops loading further pages without an error, with no "end of list" case to treat as a failure.
90	
91	## Requirements *(mandatory)*
92	
93	### Functional Requirements
94	
95	- **FR-001**: The system MUST provide a "Meus Registros" screen, reachable from the app's existing side-menu navigation, that fetches and displays all of the signed-in user's journal entries regardless of origin (manual, audio, photo, or chat).
96	- **FR-002**: Entries MUST be grouped under date headings by the calendar day they occurred ("Hoje" for today, "Ontem" for yesterday, an explicit date for anything older), with date groups ordered newest-to-oldest and, within each group, entries ordered newest-to-oldest by their occurrence time; each entry MUST be rendered as a card showing: a marker and icon distinguishing its origin, its time, a text excerpt, any attached tags as read-only chips (only when present), and a per-entry synchronization badge.
97	- **FR-003**: The system MUST support browsing the user's complete entry history beyond what fits in a single fetch, loading further entries automatically as the user scrolls, and appending them without disturbing already-rendered cards or the user's current scroll position.
98	- **FR-004**: When the signed-in user has zero entries, the screen MUST show an empty state (illustration, "Nenhum registro ainda", and a "Criar primeiro registro" action) instead of an empty list; completing a save from that action MUST return the user to this screen with the new entry visible in its correct date group.
99	- **FR-005**: The per-entry synchronization badge MUST independently reflect exactly one of three states — synchronized, synchronizing, or synchronization error — computed for each entry from its own server-confirmed data together with the device's own knowledge of any write still pending or unreconciled for that entry, following the sync-badge semantics; this computation and its on-screen state MUST NOT depend on, be blocked by, or be delayed by session or authentication handling (login, silent renewal, or the expired-session overlay).
100	- **FR-006**: Loading or refreshing this screen's data MUST check the session and silently renew it when merely expired-but-renewable, without interrupting the user, consistent with the app's existing session-renewal behavior.
101	- **FR-007**: If the session cannot be silently renewed while this screen is open, the existing "Sessão expirada" overlay MUST appear on top of it without discarding the entries already loaded or the current scroll position; once the user re-authenticates, the overlay MUST dismiss and the screen MUST be restored exactly as it was. Reconciling any single entry's state after such an event (or after any other interruption) MUST be done by re-confirming that specific entry rather than by reloading or reordering the whole list.
102	- **FR-008**: The screen's header download affordance and its search bar with funnel button MUST be rendered to match the prototype for visual fidelity, but MUST NOT perform export or search/filter behavior in this unit — those behaviors belong to later units and MUST NOT be implemented here.
103	- **FR-009**: While the device is offline, entries already loaded on this screen MUST remain visible and scrollable; attempting to load further pages MUST fail with a clear, retryable message rather than hanging or crashing, and no write of any kind MUST be attempted from this screen.
104	- **FR-010**: This unit MUST NOT implement entry search, text filtering, the category/date/type filter sheet, active-filter chips, export generation, or any other behavior reserved for a later unit (RF05, RF06, or any later RF) or for an extension feature (requirements section 2).
105	- **FR-011**: This unit MUST NOT modify the backend, its API contract, or its configuration in any way.
106	
107	### Key Entities
108	
109	- **Journal Entry**: The same persisted, immutable record introduced by RF01 — text content, a creation/occurrence time, and an origin — now also carrying the server-confirmation data (its last-confirmed-write time and the ever-increasing revision counter) and any read-only tags attached to it, and now rendered regardless of which of the four possible origins (`manual`, `audio`, `photo`, `chat`) produced it.

120	- **SC-004**: When a session expires while a user is viewing this screen, 100% of the time their loaded entries and scroll position are unchanged after they re-authenticate.

# Feature Specification: P-RF07 — Multi-source history (timeline)

**Feature Branch**: `005-multi-source-timeline` (spec directory only — no git branch was created automatically; none of this repo's extension hooks are configured)

**Created**: 2026-10-17

**Status**: Draft

**Input**: User description: "P-RF07 — Multi-source history (timeline): Show all of the user's entries in a timeline, whatever their origin, with a per-entry synchronization badge, per docs/input/requirements.md section 1 (RF07) and its acceptance criteria. Prototype states: 'Tela 4 — Meus Registros' (default) and 'Tela 4 — Vazio' (prototype extract, section 2.4); the 'Sessão expirada' overlay (section 4). Badge semantics: docs/input/backend/sync-badge.md. Backend: GET /entries, GET /entries/:id, GET /auth/session, POST /auth/refresh. Depends on F000, RF01. Do not implement features of later units, extension features (requirements section 2), or change the backend."

## Clarifications

### Session 2026-10-17

- Q: RF01 (already delivered) opens the Insertion Modal only from Home/Chat's "+" button and, on a successful save, always returns the user to Home/Chat. This unit adds a second entry point — the "Criar primeiro registro" action on this screen's empty state — so where should a save started from there return the user to, and must the newly created entry appear here immediately? → A: It returns to this screen (Meus Registros), not to Home/Chat, and the newly created entry appears immediately in its correct date group. The entire purpose of the empty-state action is to take the user from zero entries to seeing their first one; returning them to Home/Chat instead would leave the empty state looking unresolved even though the entry was created. This reuses the same in-memory entries store RF01 already appends to on a successful save (and that it documented as existing "for later units ... to read"), merged with whatever this screen has already loaded from the backend. (Resolved by technical judgment per user direction, applying Constitution Principle I.)
- Q: `GET /entries/:id` is listed under this requirement, but no entry-detail or full-text screen appears anywhere in the prototype's navigation map or navigable-state catalog for "Meus Registros" — only a card with a truncated text excerpt. What is this endpoint actually for in this unit? → A: It is not used to open a detail view (none is drawn anywhere, and inventing one would conflict with this unit's visual-fidelity obligation to the frozen prototype). Instead, this unit uses it to re-confirm the state of one specific, already-loaded entry during reconciliation — for example, after the "Sessão expirada" overlay is dismissed and the session is renewed — rather than re-fetching the entire paginated list, which is what keeps already-rendered cards and the scroll position from being disturbed, in line with this requirement's own acceptance criterion about not losing scroll position. (Resolved by technical judgment per user direction, applying Constitution Principle I.)
- Q: When this screen merges the entry RF01's save flow already placed in the app's local in-memory entries store with the entries this screen fetches from the backend, how should it avoid showing that same entry twice? → A: Dedupe by entry ID. RF01's save flow only adds an entry to the local store after the backend has confirmed the write, so every locally-held entry already carries a real, server-issued ID; when a fetched backend page returns an entry whose ID already exists in the local store, the two are recognized as the same entry and shown once (preferring the freshly-fetched copy's confirmation data — `updatedAt`/`serverRevision` — since it is at least as current as the local one). This is the simplest reliable key available and is what keeps SC-001's "100% of entries appear exactly once" true once a locally-created entry's page is later re-fetched from the backend. (Resolved by technical judgment per user direction, applying Constitution Principle I.)
- Q: Within each date group (and across date groups), in what order are entries displayed — and does that order match the order newer pages get appended to older ones while scrolling? → A: Reverse-chronological throughout: date groups run newest-to-oldest ("Hoje" at the very top), and within each group entries run newest-to-oldest by their occurrence time. This matches the backend's cursor-based pagination (each further page is strictly older than what's already loaded) and the prototype's own "Hoje"/"Ontem"/older-dates ordering, and it is the only ordering under which "scrolling down loads older entries, appended at the bottom" (FR-003, Edge Cases) is coherent without resorting already-rendered cards. Neither the prototype extract nor `requirements.md` states this explicitly, so this is a reasonable technical decision per Constitution Principle I rather than an invented behavior with no basis in the frozen inputs. (Resolved by technical judgment per user direction, applying Constitution Principle I.)

## User Scenarios & Testing *(mandatory)*

### User Story 1 - Seeing every entry in one place, regardless of how it was created (Priority: P1)

A user who has written notes, recorded audio, and captured photos over several days opens "Meus Registros" from the side menu and sees all of those entries together, in a single timeline, grouped by the day they happened ("Hoje", "Ontem", then calendar dates), each one visually marked with where it came from.

**Why this priority**: This is the entire reason the screen exists — a user's journal is split across capture methods, and without this unified view there is no way to look back at everything they've recorded.

**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by seeding a user with entries of different origins across different days, opening "Meus Registros", and confirming every entry appears exactly once, grouped under the correct date heading, with an origin-appropriate visual marker on each.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** a user with entries created as text, audio, and photo on different days, **When** they open "Meus Registros", **Then** every one of those entries appears in the list, grouped under date headings ("Hoje" for today's entries, "Ontem" for yesterday's, an explicit date for anything older), each showing a time, an origin-colored marker and icon, a text excerpt, and a synchronization badge.
2. **Given** an entry that has tags attached (from existing account data), **When** its card is rendered, **Then** those tags appear as read-only chips on the card; **given** an entry with no tags, **When** its card is rendered, **Then** no tag chips appear for it.
3. **Given** the list of entries is longer than fits on screen, **When** the user scrolls down, **Then** older entries load automatically and are appended to the list without disturbing the entries already shown or losing the user's scroll position.

---

### User Story 2 - Starting from nothing (Priority: P1)

A brand-new user, or one who has not yet created any entry, opens "Meus Registros" and sees a clear empty state instead of a blank or broken screen, with a direct path to creating their first entry.

**Why this priority**: Equally fundamental to Story 1 — this screen must handle the zero-entries case correctly from day one, since it is the state every account starts in.

**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by opening "Meus Registros" on an account with zero entries, confirming the empty-state illustration, message, and call-to-action appear, and confirming that action leads to creating an entry that then populates the screen.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** an account with no entries at all, **When** the user opens "Meus Registros", **Then** they see the empty state — a notebook illustration, the message "Nenhum registro ainda", and a "Criar primeiro registro" action — instead of an empty list.
2. **Given** the empty state is showing, **When** the user taps "Criar primeiro registro", **Then** the existing entry-creation flow opens; **when** they complete a save, **Then** they return to "Meus Registros" and see that new entry now populating the list in place of the empty state.

---

### User Story 3 - The session expires while browsing (Priority: P2)

A user is scrolled partway through their history when their backend session expires. A clear prompt to log in again appears over the screen, and once they do, they land back exactly where they were — same entries loaded, same scroll position.

**Why this priority**: An edge condition of Story 1 that protects against data loss and disorientation; it cannot be exercised until the timeline itself exists, but it is important enough to this requirement's own acceptance criteria to rank above cosmetic concerns.

**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by loading the timeline, scrolling to a known position, forcing a session-expired response, confirming the overlay appears without resetting the list, and confirming re-authentication restores that exact scroll position and content.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** the user is scrolled to a particular position in "Meus Registros", **When** the backend reports the session has expired, **Then** the "Sessão expirada" overlay appears on top of the screen without discarding the loaded entries or resetting the scroll position.
2. **Given** the overlay is visible, **When** the user re-authenticates successfully, **Then** the overlay dismisses and the screen is restored exactly as it was, without reloading or reordering the entries already on screen.

---

### User Story 4 - The synchronization badge tells the truth, even during session trouble (Priority: P3)

While a user is looking at their timeline — including while a session renewal is happening in the background, or while the "Sessão expirada" overlay is up — each entry's synchronization badge keeps showing an accurate state (synchronized, synchronizing, or sync error) and is never frozen, blanked, or delayed by whatever is happening with the session.

**Why this priority**: A correctness and trust property layered on top of Story 1's display rather than a feature of its own; it depends on the timeline and the session-expiry handling of Story 3 already existing.

**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by putting entries in each of the three badge states, forcing a session expiration and renewal in the background, and confirming every badge's state is unaffected by that session activity throughout.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** entries in each of the three synchronization states, **When** a session renewal happens silently in the background, **Then** every badge still reflects its correct, unchanged state throughout and after the renewal.
2. **Given** the "Sessão expirada" overlay is visible over the timeline, **When** the user inspects the cards underneath (e.g., once it is dismissed), **Then** every badge's state is exactly what it was before the overlay appeared, with no badge having changed, frozen, or disappeared because of the session event.

---

### Edge Cases

- The device is offline while viewing this screen: already-loaded entries remain visible and scrollable (per the product's offline behavior), but loading further pages fails with a clear, retryable message instead of hanging or crashing; no write of any kind happens from this screen.
- The backend returns an entry whose origin is `chat` — a source this app cannot yet produce (chat and "save to journal" are later units) but that `GET /entries` can still return (e.g., from seed/test data): the card renders with the origin's defined marker and icon like any other, without erroring or treating it as unrecognized.
- The most recent page of entries is itself empty (e.g., nothing happened today or yesterday) while the account has entries further back: paging continues to load those older groups rather than showing the empty state, which is reserved for a true zero-entries account.
- A page load fails outright (not just going offline mid-session): the user sees a clear, retryable loading error for that page without losing or corrupting the entries already shown above it.
- The user reaches the end of their history: the list simply stops loading further pages without an error, with no "end of list" case to treat as a failure.

## Requirements *(mandatory)*

### Functional Requirements

- **FR-001**: The system MUST provide a "Meus Registros" screen, reachable from the app's existing side-menu navigation, that fetches and displays all of the signed-in user's journal entries regardless of origin (manual, audio, photo, or chat).
- **FR-002**: Entries MUST be grouped under date headings by the calendar day they occurred ("Hoje" for today, "Ontem" for yesterday, an explicit date for anything older), with date groups ordered newest-to-oldest and, within each group, entries ordered newest-to-oldest by their occurrence time; each entry MUST be rendered as a card showing: a marker and icon distinguishing its origin, its time, a text excerpt, any attached tags as read-only chips (only when present), and a per-entry synchronization badge.
- **FR-003**: The system MUST support browsing the user's complete entry history beyond what fits in a single fetch, loading further entries automatically as the user scrolls, and appending them without disturbing already-rendered cards or the user's current scroll position.
- **FR-004**: When the signed-in user has zero entries, the screen MUST show an empty state (illustration, "Nenhum registro ainda", and a "Criar primeiro registro" action) instead of an empty list; completing a save from that action MUST return the user to this screen with the new entry visible in its correct date group.
- **FR-005**: The per-entry synchronization badge MUST independently reflect exactly one of three states — synchronized, synchronizing, or synchronization error — computed for each entry from its own server-confirmed data together with the device's own knowledge of any write still pending or unreconciled for that entry, following the sync-badge semantics; this computation and its on-screen state MUST NOT depend on, be blocked by, or be delayed by session or authentication handling (login, silent renewal, or the expired-session overlay).
- **FR-006**: Loading or refreshing this screen's data MUST check the session and silently renew it when merely expired-but-renewable, without interrupting the user, consistent with the app's existing session-renewal behavior.
- **FR-007**: If the session cannot be silently renewed while this screen is open, the existing "Sessão expirada" overlay MUST appear on top of it without discarding the entries already loaded or the current scroll position; once the user re-authenticates, the overlay MUST dismiss and the screen MUST be restored exactly as it was. Reconciling any single entry's state after such an event (or after any other interruption) MUST be done by re-confirming that specific entry rather than by reloading or reordering the whole list.
- **FR-008**: The screen's header download affordance and its search bar with funnel button MUST be rendered to match the prototype for visual fidelity, but MUST NOT perform export or search/filter behavior in this unit — those behaviors belong to later units and MUST NOT be implemented here.
- **FR-009**: While the device is offline, entries already loaded on this screen MUST remain visible and scrollable; attempting to load further pages MUST fail with a clear, retryable message rather than hanging or crashing, and no write of any kind MUST be attempted from this screen.
- **FR-010**: This unit MUST NOT implement entry search, text filtering, the category/date/type filter sheet, active-filter chips, export generation, or any other behavior reserved for a later unit (RF05, RF06, or any later RF) or for an extension feature (requirements section 2).
- **FR-011**: This unit MUST NOT modify the backend, its API contract, or its configuration in any way.

### Key Entities

- **Journal Entry**: The same persisted, immutable record introduced by RF01 — text content, a creation/occurrence time, and an origin — now also carrying the server-confirmation data (its last-confirmed-write time and the ever-increasing revision counter) and any read-only tags attached to it, and now rendered regardless of which of the four possible origins (`manual`, `audio`, `photo`, `chat`) produced it.
- **Synchronization Badge State**: A derived, per-entry value — synchronized, synchronizing, or synchronization error — computed entirely on the device from an entry's own confirmation data and the device's own record of any write for that entry still pending or unreconciled; never itself stored by or requested directly from the backend.
- **Entry Timeline Page**: The windowed view of the user's full entry history currently loaded on screen — the entries fetched so far and the position to continue from — preserved across scrolling, backgrounding, and a session expiration/renewal cycle so the user's place is never lost.

## Success Criteria *(mandatory)*

### Measurable Outcomes

- **SC-001**: 100% of a user's entries — across every origin they've used — appear exactly once in the timeline (including an entry created via this screen's own empty-state flow that a later backend fetch also returns, de-duplicated by entry ID), correctly grouped by the day they occurred, with no entry requiring the user to know or remember which capture method created it.
- **SC-002**: 100% of accounts with zero entries see the empty state with a working path into creating their first entry, never a blank, broken, or perpetually-loading screen.
- **SC-003**: Users can scroll through their entire entry history, however long, with additional entries loading automatically in every case, without ever needing a manual "load more" action or losing their scroll position.
- **SC-004**: When a session expires while a user is viewing this screen, 100% of the time their loaded entries and scroll position are unchanged after they re-authenticate.
- **SC-005**: Every entry visible on screen shows one of the three defined synchronization states at all times, unaffected by whatever is happening with the user's session at that moment.

## Assumptions

- The header's download icon and the search bar with its funnel button are rendered to match the prototype (visual fidelity) but are inert placeholders in this unit; their behavior belongs to RF05 (export) and RF06 (search/filter), both later in the delivery order.
- No entry can currently be created with origin `chat` (RF04's chat and RF10's "save to journal" are later units), but because `GET /entries` is origin-agnostic and the prototype's component library already defines a visual treatment for all four origins, this screen renders `chat`-origin entries correctly if the backend ever returns one (e.g., from seed data) rather than treating it as an error case.
- This unit introduces no new local database. It reuses the in-memory entries store RF01 already created and documented as available for later units to read, merging it with the entries this screen fetches and paginates from the backend, de-duplicated by entry ID (see the resolved Clarification on this merge) so an entry created via this screen's own empty-state flow is never shown twice once a later backend fetch also returns it.
- The "synchronizing" and "synchronization error" badge states are implemented completely and correctly per `docs/input/backend/sync-badge.md`, and must respond correctly to whatever pending or failed local write state exists for an entry. Because RF01's existing save flow only ever makes an entry visible anywhere after the backend has already confirmed it, these two states may rarely or never be observed through today's own capture flow alone — that does not make their correct implementation optional, since the requirement's acceptance criterion is about the badge's independence from the authentication stream, not about how often each state is exercised by this unit's own flows.
- Date-heading grouping ("Hoje", "Ontem", explicit dates) uses the device's local calendar day applied to each entry's occurrence timestamp, matching the prototype's labels.
- No entry-detail or full-text screen is introduced in this unit — see the resolved Clarification on `GET /entries/:id`'s purpose; a card's text excerpt is the only rendering of an entry's content here.
- "No BLoC imports another BLoC directly" (the requirement's own architecture-level acceptance criterion) is carried forward as an implementation-time constraint for the planning phase; at the specification level it is expressed through FR-005's and FR-007's independence requirements between the synchronization badge and session/authentication handling.

1	# Data Model: P-RF07 — Multi-source history (timeline)
2	
3	Source: spec.md §Key Entities, requirements.md §§1 (RF07), 6.2, 8, 13; `docs/input/backend/sync-badge.md`;
4	`docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml`'s `/entries` (list) and `/entries/{id}` schemas;
5	`docs/input/prototype/prototype-extract.md` §§2.4, 3, 6. This unit extends the `entries` feature's shared
6	`Entry`/`EntriesRepository` (RF01) with two new read methods, and adds one new feature folder's worth of
7	domain helpers and presentation (`records/`, R8) — it introduces no new backend-shaped entity beyond widening
8	one existing enum (R2).
9	
10	## `Entry` (`lib/features/entries/domain/entities/entry.dart`) — extended, not replaced
11	
12	Every field RF01 already modeled (`id`, `content`, `source`, `chatMessageId`, `occurredAt`, `tags`,
13	`piiStatus`, `piiSpans`, `embeddingStatus`, `mediaDurationSeconds`, `serverRevision`, `createdAt`, `updatedAt`)
14	is unchanged in shape — this unit reads `serverRevision`/`updatedAt` (sync-badge.md's two fields) and `tags`
15	(read-only chips), which RF01 already carries but never renders. One change:
16	
17	```dart
18	enum EntrySource { manual, audio, photo, chat }   // chat added (research.md R2)
19	```
20	
21	## `EntriesPage` (`lib/features/entries/domain/entities/entries_page.dart`) — NEW
22	
23	The shape of one `GET /entries` response, minus the fields this unit never uses (`meta.total`, and every
24	`source`/`dateFrom`/`dateTo` filter parameter — reserved for RF06).
25	
26	| Field | Type | Notes |
27	|---|---|---|
28	| `entries` | `List<Entry>` | `data`, in the order the backend returns it (newest-occurred-first, per the resolved ordering Clarification). |
29	| `nextCursor` | `String?` | `meta.nextCursor` verbatim; `null` means this was the last page. |
30	
31	```dart
32	class EntriesPage extends Equatable {
33	  const EntriesPage({required this.entries, required this.nextCursor});
34	  final List<Entry> entries;
35	  final String? nextCursor;
36	}
37	```
38	
39	## `EntriesRepository` — extended (`lib/features/entries/domain/repositories/entries_repository.dart`)
40	
41	```dart
42	abstract class EntriesRepository {
43	  Future<Either<Failure, Entry>> create({required String content, required EntrySource source}); // unchanged (RF01)
44	  List<Entry> get cachedEntries;                                                                   // unchanged (RF01)
45	  Future<Either<Failure, EntriesPage>> list({String? cursor});                                      // NEW
46	  Future<Either<Failure, Entry>> getById(String id);                                                // NEW
47	}
48	```
49	
50	- **`list`** → `GET /entries` (`entries-list`), query parameters `cursor` (when non-null) only — no `limit`
51	  override (backend default 20), no `source`/`dateFrom`/`dateTo` (filters are RF06's).
52	- **`getById`** → `GET /entries/:id` (`entries-get`), `pathSegments: [id]`. Implemented and tested; no call
53	  site in this unit's UI flow (research.md R7).
54	- Both retry exactly once through `SessionRepository.refresh()` on `AuthExpiredFailure` before giving up
55	  (research.md R4) — see `contracts/entries-repository-extension.md` for the exact sequence. `create()` is
56	  untouched.

59

61	`_parseEntry` the existing `create()` already uses (made reusable across a single object and a list of
62	objects) — no duplicated parsing logic. `list()` additionally parses `meta.nextCursor`.

65	
66	Gains one new constructor dependency: `SessionRepository` (`session/domain/repositories/session_repository.dart`
67	— a cross-feature *domain* interface, the same shape `SessionRepositoryImpl` already depends on `auth`'s

71	
72	```dart
73	Future<Either<Failure, Map<String, dynamic>>> call(
74	  String function, {
75	  required String method,
76	  Map<String, dynamic>? body,
77	  List<String>? pathSegments,
78	  Map<String, dynamic>? queryParameters,   // NEW (research.md R1)

87

89	enum SyncBadgeState { synchronized, synchronizing, error }
90	enum LocalWriteOutcome { pending, failed }
91	
92	class SyncBadge {
93	  const SyncBadge._();
94	  static SyncBadgeState derive(LocalWriteOutcome? localWrite) => switch (localWrite) {
95	    null => SyncBadgeState.synchronized,
96	    LocalWriteOutcome.pending => SyncBadgeState.synchronizing,

100	```

108	verbatim, no new token):
109	
110	| `SyncBadgeState` | Dot color | Label |
111	|---|---|---|
112	| `synchronized` | `DesignTokens.colorSuccess` (`#4C6B4F`) | "sincronizado" |
113	| `synchronizing` | `DesignTokens.colorWarningSync` (`#C98A3E`) | "sincronizando" |

124	  final String label;            // "Hoje" | "Ontem" | "{day} de {monthName}" (research.md R9)
125	  final List<Entry> entries;     // newest-to-oldest by occurredAt (resolved ordering Clarification)
126	}

# Data Model: P-RF07 — Multi-source history (timeline)

Source: spec.md §Key Entities, requirements.md §§1 (RF07), 6.2, 8, 13; `docs/input/backend/sync-badge.md`;
`docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml`'s `/entries` (list) and `/entries/{id}` schemas;
`docs/input/prototype/prototype-extract.md` §§2.4, 3, 6. This unit extends the `entries` feature's shared
`Entry`/`EntriesRepository` (RF01) with two new read methods, and adds one new feature folder's worth of
domain helpers and presentation (`records/`, R8) — it introduces no new backend-shaped entity beyond widening
one existing enum (R2).

## `Entry` (`lib/features/entries/domain/entities/entry.dart`) — extended, not replaced

Every field RF01 already modeled (`id`, `content`, `source`, `chatMessageId`, `occurredAt`, `tags`,
`piiStatus`, `piiSpans`, `embeddingStatus`, `mediaDurationSeconds`, `serverRevision`, `createdAt`, `updatedAt`)
is unchanged in shape — this unit reads `serverRevision`/`updatedAt` (sync-badge.md's two fields) and `tags`
(read-only chips), which RF01 already carries but never renders. One change:

```dart
enum EntrySource { manual, audio, photo, chat }   // chat added (research.md R2)
```

## `EntriesPage` (`lib/features/entries/domain/entities/entries_page.dart`) — NEW

The shape of one `GET /entries` response, minus the fields this unit never uses (`meta.total`, and every
`source`/`dateFrom`/`dateTo` filter parameter — reserved for RF06).

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `entries` | `List<Entry>` | `data`, in the order the backend returns it (newest-occurred-first, per the resolved ordering Clarification). |
| `nextCursor` | `String?` | `meta.nextCursor` verbatim; `null` means this was the last page. |

```dart
class EntriesPage extends Equatable {
  const EntriesPage({required this.entries, required this.nextCursor});
  final List<Entry> entries;
  final String? nextCursor;
}
```

## `EntriesRepository` — extended (`lib/features/entries/domain/repositories/entries_repository.dart`)

```dart
abstract class EntriesRepository {
  Future<Either<Failure, Entry>> create({required String content, required EntrySource source}); // unchanged (RF01)
  List<Entry> get cachedEntries;                                                                   // unchanged (RF01)
  Future<Either<Failure, EntriesPage>> list({String? cursor});                                      // NEW
  Future<Either<Failure, Entry>> getById(String id);                                                // NEW
}
```

- **`list`** → `GET /entries` (`entries-list`), query parameters `cursor` (when non-null) only — no `limit`
  override (backend default 20), no `source`/`dateFrom`/`dateTo` (filters are RF06's).
- **`getById`** → `GET /entries/:id` (`entries-get`), `pathSegments: [id]`. Implemented and tested; no call
  site in this unit's UI flow (research.md R7).
- Both retry exactly once through `SessionRepository.refresh()` on `AuthExpiredFailure` before giving up
  (research.md R4) — see `contracts/entries-repository-extension.md` for the exact sequence. `create()` is
  untouched.

### `EntriesRemoteDataSource` — extended (`lib/features/entries/data/entries_remote_data_source.dart`)

Adds `list({String? cursor})` and `getById(String id)`, both parsing responses through the *same* private
`_parseEntry` the existing `create()` already uses (made reusable across a single object and a list of
objects) — no duplicated parsing logic. `list()` additionally parses `meta.nextCursor`.

### `EntriesRepositoryImpl` — extended (`lib/features/entries/data/entries_repository_impl.dart`)

Gains one new constructor dependency: `SessionRepository` (`session/domain/repositories/session_repository.dart`
— a cross-feature *domain* interface, the same shape `SessionRepositoryImpl` already depends on `auth`'s
`Account`). `cachedEntries`/`create()` behavior is unchanged.

## `ApiClient` — extended (`lib/core/network/api_client.dart`)

```dart
Future<Either<Failure, Map<String, dynamic>>> call(
  String function, {
  required String method,
  Map<String, dynamic>? body,
  List<String>? pathSegments,
  Map<String, dynamic>? queryParameters,   // NEW (research.md R1)
  AuthMode authMode = AuthMode.userSession,
})
```

`queryParameters` is passed straight through to `Dio.request()`. Every existing call site (`entries-create`,
`auth-session`, `auth-refresh`, `media-ocr`) is unaffected — the parameter defaults to omitted.

## `SyncBadgeState` / `LocalWriteOutcome` (`lib/features/records/domain/entities/sync_badge_state.dart`) — NEW

```dart
enum SyncBadgeState { synchronized, synchronizing, error }
enum LocalWriteOutcome { pending, failed }

class SyncBadge {
  const SyncBadge._();
  static SyncBadgeState derive(LocalWriteOutcome? localWrite) => switch (localWrite) {
    null => SyncBadgeState.synchronized,
    LocalWriteOutcome.pending => SyncBadgeState.synchronizing,
    LocalWriteOutcome.failed => SyncBadgeState.error,
  };
}
```

A pure, total function over `sync-badge.md`'s model (research.md R6). `RecordsBloc` calls it with
`localWrite: null` for every entry it ever renders — both of its entry sources (`EntriesRepository.list()`'s
results, `.cachedEntries`) are, by construction, already server-confirmed. Never depends on session/auth state
(FR-005), by having no session-related input at all.

**Mapping to the prototype's sync badge** (`prototype-extract.md` §3/§6 — reuses existing `DesignTokens`
verbatim, no new token):

| `SyncBadgeState` | Dot color | Label |
|---|---|---|
| `synchronized` | `DesignTokens.colorSuccess` (`#4C6B4F`) | "sincronizado" |
| `synchronizing` | `DesignTokens.colorWarningSync` (`#C98A3E`) | "sincronizando" |
| `error` | `DesignTokens.colorError` (`#B3402A`) | "erro de sync" |

## `DateGroup` / `DateGrouper` (`lib/features/records/domain/entities/date_group.dart`) — NEW

Maps spec.md's "Entry Timeline Page" grouping requirement (FR-002) to a pure function, independent of widget
code so it's directly unit-testable (RNF07).

```dart
class DateGroup extends Equatable {
  const DateGroup({required this.label, required this.entries});
  final String label;            // "Hoje" | "Ontem" | "{day} de {monthName}" (research.md R9)
  final List<Entry> entries;     // newest-to-oldest by occurredAt (resolved ordering Clarification)
}

class DateGrouper {
  const DateGrouper._();
  static List<DateGroup> group(List<Entry> entries, {DateTime? now});
}
```

- Input `entries` is assumed already sorted newest-to-oldest (see `EntryMerger` below, which guarantees this
  for `RecordsBloc`'s own data) — `group()` only buckets, it never re-sorts within or across groups.
  Groups themselves come out newest-to-oldest because the input is.
- Bucketing compares each entry's `occurredAt.toLocal()` calendar day against `(now ?? DateTime.now()).toLocal()`'s —
  the device's local calendar day (spec.md Assumptions), not UTC.
- `now` is an optional override purely for deterministic unit tests ("today" fixed at a known instant); production call sites omit it.

## `EntryMerger` (`lib/features/records/domain/entities/entry_merger.dart`) — NEW

Implements spec.md's resolved Clarification 3 (dedupe-by-ID, preferring the fresher copy).

```dart
class EntryMerger {
  const EntryMerger._();
  static List<Entry> merge({required List<Entry> primary, required List<Entry> secondary}) {
    // union by id, primary's copy wins on a shared id, result sorted newest-to-oldest by occurredAt
  }
}
```

`RecordsBloc` calls `EntryMerger.merge(primary: <freshly fetched or already-displayed entries>, secondary:
entriesRepository.cachedEntries)` every time it has a new batch to show (research.md R3) — never inside
`EntriesRepositoryImpl`.

## `RecordsEvent` (`lib/features/records/presentation/bloc/records_event.dart`) — NEW

| Event | When |
|---|---|
| `RecordsStarted` | `RecordsPage.initState` — triggers the first page fetch. |
| `NextPageRequested` | The list's `ScrollController` crosses a near-bottom threshold, and `!hasReachedEnd && !isLoadingMore`. |
| `PageLoadRetried` | The user taps "Tentar novamente" on a failed first load (`RecordsLoadFailure`) or a failed further-page load (`RecordsLoaded.pageLoadFailure`). |
| `RecordsLocalCacheRefreshed` | `RecordsPage`, once the insertion-modal `showModalBottomSheet` future resolves (research.md R10) — re-merges `cachedEntries` into the currently displayed list, no network call. |

## `RecordsState` (`lib/features/records/presentation/bloc/records_state.dart`) — NEW

Maps spec.md's "Entry Timeline Page" key entity directly to this sealed state's `RecordsLoaded` fields
(entries fetched so far + the cursor to continue from) — no separate domain class for it (research.md-style
reasonable decision: nothing else needs this shape outside the bloc that owns it).

```dart
sealed class RecordsState {}

class RecordsLoading extends RecordsState {}

class RecordsLoadFailure extends RecordsState {
  const RecordsLoadFailure(this.failure);
  final Failure failure;   // any failure type, including AuthExpiredFailure (research.md — see below)
}

class RecordsLoaded extends RecordsState {
  const RecordsLoaded({
    required this.entries,        // merged + deduped, newest-to-oldest
    required this.nextCursor,
    required this.isLoadingMore,
    this.pageLoadFailure,         // a further-page fetch failed; entries above stay intact, retryable
  });
  final List<Entry> entries;
  final String? nextCursor;
  final bool isLoadingMore;
  final Failure? pageLoadFailure;

  bool get hasReachedEnd => nextCursor == null;
  bool get isEmpty => entries.isEmpty;   // RecordsPage renders "Vazio" for this, never a separate event
}
```

- **First-load failure, any cause (including `AuthExpiredFailure`)** → `RecordsLoadFailure` — never the empty
  state, so a true zero-entries account is never confused with "couldn't load" (research.md's reasoning under
  R5/R7). The one-shot `reauthRequired` stream (next section) still fires in the `AuthExpiredFailure` case, on
  top of this state — the overlay appears over the retryable error screen.
- **Further-page failure, `AuthExpiredFailure`** → `entries`/`nextCursor` are left exactly as they were,
  `isLoadingMore` resets to `false` (so the next scroll-near-bottom re-attempts the same, unconsumed cursor);
  `pageLoadFailure` is **not** set for this case — only the one-shot stream fires. This is what makes FR-007's
  "without discarding the entries already loaded or the current scroll position... restored exactly as it
  was" true by construction (nothing in `RecordsState` changed).
- **Further-page failure, any other cause** (timeout, offline, validation, ...) → `pageLoadFailure` set,
  `isLoadingMore` resets to `false`, entries unchanged — a retryable inline banner at the bottom of the list
  (FR-009/Edge Cases).

## `RecordsBloc` (`lib/features/records/presentation/bloc/records_bloc.dart`) — NEW

```dart
class RecordsBloc extends Bloc<RecordsEvent, RecordsState> {
  RecordsBloc({required EntriesRepository entriesRepository});

  Stream<void> get reauthRequired;   // one-shot (research.md R5) — fired on a post-retry AuthExpiredFailure
}
```

Depends only on `EntriesRepository` (never `SessionRepository`, never `ConnectivityChecker` — research.md
R4/R11) — the one domain-layer dependency this bloc needs. Never imports `SessionBloc` or any of its
event/state types (requirements.md RF07's own acceptance criterion).

## Widgets (`lib/features/records/presentation/widgets/`, `pages/records_page.dart`) — NEW

Not separately contracted (pure prototype-fidelity rendering, no new state/logic beyond what's above):

- `records_page.dart` — `Scaffold` with the prototype's header (back arrow, title, inert download icon —
  FR-008), inert search bar + funnel button (FR-008), a `ListView` driven by `RecordsLoaded.entries` grouped
  through `DateGrouper`, a `ScrollController` that survives `BlocBuilder` rebuilds (never recreated, so scroll
  position is never lost — FR-003/FR-007), and the `reauthRequired` subscription (research.md R5).
- `record_card.dart` — one entry: spine + icon colored by `source` (table below), monospace time
  (`occurredAt.toLocal()`, `HH:mm`), `SyncBadgeDot` (table above), text excerpt (`content`, no truncation logic
  beyond what the card's fixed layout naturally clips), tag chips (`EntryTag.name`, only when `tags.isNotEmpty`
  — FR-002/Acceptance Scenario 2).
- `records_empty_state.dart` — notebook icon, "Nenhum registro ainda", "Criar primeiro registro" button
  calling the shared `openInsertionModal()` (research.md R10).
- `sync_badge_dot.dart` — the 8px dot + mono label pair, parameterized by `SyncBadgeState`.

**Origin marker mapping** (`prototype-extract.md`'s `sourceMeta`, verbatim hex — reuses existing `DesignTokens`,
no new color token; Phosphor icon names mapped to this app's existing Material-icon convention, same mapping
style RF01/RF02 already used for their own icons):

| `EntrySource` | Spine/icon color | Material icon (Phosphor equivalent) |
|---|---|---|
| `manual` | `DesignTokens.colorPrimary` (`#1F3D34`) | `Icons.edit_outlined` (`ph-pencil-simple`) |
| `audio` | `DesignTokens.colorSecondary` (`#7C8B6F`) | `Icons.mic_none` (`ph-microphone`) |
| `photo` | `DesignTokens.colorTextSecondary` (`#6B6255`) | `Icons.image_outlined` (`ph-image`) |
| `chat` | `DesignTokens.colorAccent` (`#C98A3E`) | `Icons.chat_bubble_outline` (`ph-chat-circle-text`) |

## Routing / DI changes

- `lib/core/routing/app_router.dart`: `AppRoutes.records`'s builder wraps `RecordsPage` in
  `BlocProvider<RecordsBloc>(create: (_) => getIt<RecordsBloc>()..add(const RecordsStarted()))`, replacing the

1	# Research: P-RF07 — Multi-source history (timeline)
2	
3	All unknowns below are implementation judgment calls on top of an already-resolved spec (spec.md's four
4	Clarifications) and an already-built F000/RF01 foundation — there is no new external service to evaluate, and
5	only one small, well-known package decision (rejected, R9). Each entry either extends an existing RF01/F000
6	seam to a new, previously-unneeded shape, or fills a gap spec.md leaves to "reasonable technical decision"
7	(Constitution Principle I).
8	
9	## R1 — `ApiClient` gains query-parameter support
10	
11	- **Decision**: `ApiClient.call()` gets one new optional parameter, `Map<String, dynamic>? queryParameters`,
12	  passed straight through to `Dio.request()`'s own `queryParameters` argument. Every existing call site is
13	  unaffected (the parameter defaults to omitted/null).
14	- **Rationale**: `GET /entries` (`entries-list`) is this unit's first call whose OpenAPI contract defines
15	  `in: query` parameters (`cursor`, `limit`, plus `source`/`dateFrom`/`dateTo` this unit never sends). Every
16	  endpoint called before this unit (`entries-create`, `auth-session`, `auth-refresh`, `media-ocr`) needed only a
17	  body and/or `pathSegments`, so `ApiClient` never had a reason to carry query parameters. This is a change to
18	  the app's own HTTP wrapper, not to the backend or its contract (Constitution Principle III is about the
19	  backend's contract, not this client-side plumbing).
20	- **Alternatives considered**: Hand-building the query string and appending it to the URL — rejected: `dio`
21	  already does this correctly (encoding, `null`-param omission), and bypassing it would be duplicating
22	  something the dependency already does for free.
23	
24	## R2 — `EntrySource` gains a fourth value, `chat`
25	
26	- **Decision**: `enum EntrySource { manual, audio, photo, chat }` in `entries/domain/entities/entry.dart` —
27	  the one line RF01's own comment flagged as "`chat` is RF10's own addition" is now wrong in isolation and
28	  gets updated to explain *why* a fourth value exists here even though no capture flow produces it yet.
29	- **Rationale**: spec.md's Edge Cases and Assumptions are explicit: `GET /entries` is origin-agnostic and can
30	  return a `chat`-sourced entry (e.g., from seed/test data) even though RF04/RF10 (the only features that will
31	  ever *create* one) are both later units; this screen "renders the card with the origin's defined marker and
32	  icon like any other, without erroring or treating it as unrecognized." `EntriesRemoteDataSource._parseEntry`
33	  currently calls `EntrySource.values.byName(...)`, which throws `ArgumentError` — not caught by its existing
34	  `on TypeError`/`on FormatException` clauses — for any value outside the enum's current 3. Without this
35	  change, a `chat` entry from the backend would crash parsing instead of rendering, directly contradicting the
36	  Edge Case. No other `Entry` field changes; `serverRevision`/`updatedAt` are already present from RF01 and
37	  are exactly `sync-badge.md`'s two fields.
38	- **Alternatives considered**: Leaving the enum at 3 values and adding a defensive `on ArgumentError` catch
39	  that falls back to some generic/"unknown" rendering — rejected: the OpenAPI contract closes the `source`
40	  enum at exactly 4 values (`manual`/`audio`/`photo`/`chat`), so there is no fifth value to defend against;
41	  adding a catch-all for a case that cannot occur per the frozen contract would be exactly the kind of
42	  speculative error handling the project's own guidance says to avoid.
43	
44	## R3 — Local-cache ∪ fetched-page merge lives in the `records` feature, not `EntriesRepositoryImpl`
45	
46	- **Decision**: `EntriesRepositoryImpl` gains `list()`/`getById()` as plain fetch methods — neither one reads
47	  nor touches `cachedEntries`. The by-ID dedupe spec.md's Clarification 3 resolves (prefer the freshly-fetched
48	  copy's `updatedAt`/`serverRevision` when the same ID appears in both the local cache and a fetched page) is
49	  implemented once, as a small pure function (`EntryMerger`, data-model.md) inside the new `records/domain/`,
50	  and called by `RecordsBloc` every time it has a new batch of entries to show.
51	- **Rationale**: `cachedEntries`'s own doc comment already says it exists only "so RF07 has something to read

  passed straight through to `Dio.request()`'s own `queryParameters` argument. Every existing call site is
  unaffected (the parameter defaults to omitted/null).

  `in: query` parameters (`cursor`, `limit`, plus `source`/`dateFrom`/`dateTo` this unit never sends). Every
  endpoint called before this unit (`entries-create`, `auth-session`, `auth-refresh`, `media-ocr`) needed only a
  body and/or `pathSegments`, so `ApiClient` never had a reason to carry query parameters. This is a change to
  the app's own HTTP wrapper, not to the backend or its contract (Constitution Principle III is about the
  backend's contract, not this client-side plumbing).

  already does this correctly (encoding, `null`-param omission), and bypassing it would be duplicating
  something the dependency already does for free.

  gets updated to explain *why* a fourth value exists here even though no capture flow produces it yet.
